The correct mathematical concept being applied in the "CountingFriends" task is combinations. Specifically, it involves calculating the number of ways to choose 10 people from a group of 10 friends without regard to the order of selection.

In this problem, since Peter needs to choose all 10 friends and there are exactly 10 friends available, there is only one way to form the team. This can be represented mathematically using the combination formula \( C(n, k) = \frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!} \), where \( n \) is the total number of items (friends in this case), and \( k \) is the number of items to choose.

For Peter's situation:
\[ C(10, 10) = \frac{10!}{10!(10-10)!} = \frac{10!}{10! \cdot 0!} = 1 \]

Thus, there is only one choice for forming the team, which corresponds to answer choice B) 1.
